reviews.body: Ran the new test setup (AirPassengersPanel, 6 masked rows per series) with local_scaler_type="standard" on this branch and printed nf.scalers_["y"].stats_.

review_comments.body: The fit works now, but the zeros go into the local scaler fit, since `_scalers_fit_transform` uses the whole column and coreforecast's scalers aren't NaN-aware. Series 2 gets mean 557.5 / std 166.6 vs 581.8 / 121.9 on its observed rows (std +37%), so every series with a masked gap is scaled differently from the same series without it. Would it be worth fitting the scalers on the available rows only, or filling with something that doesn't move the stats?

comments.body:
Thanks for running this and for the numbers. You're right: filling masked rows with zeros fixes the crash, but those zeros still enter the local scaler fit, so any series with a gap gets different stats than it would without it.

Two options: (a) fit the scalers only on rows where the mask is observed, or (b) keep the fill but exclude the filled rows from the stats. Both touch how `_scalers_fit_transform` is called, so we'd like a maintainer's view on which they prefer before changing it in this PR.
